answer: In an agent market selling fable manuscripts, ivory paint, and cedar furniture, each seller identity must lock $100 for 30 days before accepting orders, with only one order worth at most $20 open at a time. Creating accounts is cheap, but activating 10,000 sellers ties up $1 million. Splitting across identities cannot evade the collateral requirement: every extra $20 of simultaneous selling capacity requires another $100 locked away.
